import pytest
from solution import format_table


def test_exact_example():
    out = format_table([[1, "hi"], [22, "world!"]], ["n", "word"], max_col_width=5)
    expected = (
        "+----+-------+\n"
        "| n  | word  |\n"
        "+----+-------+\n"
        "| 1  | hi    |\n"
        "| 22 | world |\n"
        "|    | !     |\n"
        "+----+-------+"
    )
    assert out == expected


def test_header_wider_than_data():
    out = format_table([["a"]], ["header"])
    assert "| header |" in out
    assert "| a      |" in out

    out = format_table([["ab\ncdef"]], ["h"], max_col_width=3)
    lines = out.split("\n")
    assert lines[3] == "| ab  |"
    assert lines[4] == "| cde |"
    assert lines[5] == "| f   |"

content.text: The cause is an off-by-one in the cell width arithmetic. `widths[c]` is the content width, and the border uses `w + 2`, so each cell's content area should be exactly `w` characters. Two places use `w - 1` instead: `_cell_lines` wraps at `width - 1`, and `_align` pads to `width - len - 1`. I'll fix both.

The cause was an off-by-one in the cell width arithmetic: the column width `w` is the content width, and the borders are drawn `w + 2` wide, so each cell should hold exactly `w` characters. `_cell_lines` wrapped text at `width - 1`, which caused the extra wrapped rows ("header" split into "heade" and "r", and "cdef" split too early). `_align` padded to `width - len - 1`, which left one column short ("n" rendered as " n " in a width-2 column). I changed the wrap condition to `len(line) > width` and the padding to `width - len(text)`. The public API (`format_table`) is unchanged, and nothing under `tests/` was touched.
